title: Sleeper Agents: Training Deceptive LLMs that Persist Through Safety Training
summary: Constructs triggered deceptive behaviors and tests whether common safety-training methods remove them.
caveat: The backdoors are deliberately trained; persistence in this experiment does not prove spontaneous deceptive alignment.
review_scope: Primary-page metadata and abstract checked; findings not independently replicated and full methods not audited.

title: AI Control: Improving Safety Despite Intentional Subversion
summary: Tests protocols that combine trusted resources and untrusted models to reduce harmful outcomes even when the untrusted model is trying to subvert the process.
caveat: The evaluated programming-task threat model is deliberately restricted; results do not guarantee control of arbitrary future systems.
review_scope: Primary-page metadata and abstract checked; findings not independently replicated and full methods not audited.

title: Scalable Extraction of Training Data from (Production) Language Models
summary: Studies extraction of memorized training data from several types of language models, highlighting privacy risks that behavior alignment alone does not remove.
caveat: Results concern model versions and query conditions tested at the time; current service behavior may differ.
review_scope: Primary-page metadata and abstract checked; findings not independently replicated and full methods not audited.

title: Universal and Transferable Adversarial Attacks on Aligned Language Models
summary: Demonstrates automated adversarial prompt patterns that can transfer between some aligned language models.
caveat: Transfer rates are model- and version-dependent; this catalog does not reproduce operational attack payloads.
review_scope: Primary-page metadata and abstract checked; findings not independently replicated and full methods not audited.

title: Not what you've signed up for: Compromising Real-World LLM-Integrated Applications with Indirect Prompt Injection
summary: Shows how attacker-controlled retrieved content can be treated as instructions by an LLM application, crossing the intended trust boundary.
caveat: Specific demonstrations are historical; the general data-versus-instruction boundary remains the important design issue.
review_scope: Primary-page metadata and abstract checked; findings not independently replicated and full methods not audited.
